questions.subject: Social Science
questions.stem: A government has completed the term for which it was chosen. Explain, in about 45 words, why it cannot carry on in office without seeking the mandate of the people again.

markingPoints.description: Periodic elections named as one of the most crucial elements of democracy (1)
Citizens must participate in choosing those who will make decisions on their behalf (1)
Elected representatives are accountable to the people, and periodic elections ensure that accountability (1)

answerScheme.modelAnswer: Periodic elections are among the most crucial elements of democracy, because citizens must take part in choosing those who will make decisions on their behalf. Elected representatives are accountable to the people, and holding them accountable is ensured through periodic elections. A government that carries on beyond its prescribed term denies the people the chance to renew or withhold that mandate.

questions.stem: A student argues that casting a vote once is all that citizens owe, since their representatives have already been chosen. In about 45 words, explain what the right to elect representatives really involves and how periodic elections make it meaningful.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.stem: Gurmat was elected class representative in Grade 8. The class now asks whether she may carry on as the class representative in Grade 9 without facing a fresh election, and whether a government may similarly carry on beyond its prescribed term without seeking the mandate of the people again. Answer both, giving your reasons in steps.

markingPoints.description: A fresh election required before Gurmat carries on as the class representative in Grade 9 (1)
A government cannot carry on beyond the prescribed term without seeking the mandate of the people again (1)
Participating in the periodic election of those who will make decisions on our behalf named as one of the most crucial elements of democracy (1)
Elected representatives are accountable to the people (1)
Periodic elections ensure that accountability, and our vote is the principal means of exercising the right (1)

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
Step 1 - No, Gurmat cannot carry on as the class representative in Grade 9 without facing a fresh election.
Step 2 - The answer is No for a government as well: it cannot carry on beyond the prescribed term without seeking the mandate of the people again.
Step 3 - The reason is that participating in the periodic election of those who will make decisions on our behalf is one of the most crucial elements of democracy.
Step 4 - Elected representatives are accountable to the people.
Step 5 - Periodic elections are what ensure that accountability, and our vote is the principal means by which we exercise the right to elect and hold them accountable.

Step 2 - The right to elect our representatives also involves holding them accountable.
Step 3 - Holding them accountable is ensured through periodic elections, and our vote is the principal means by which we exercise this right.
Step 4 - So the vote lets the people renew, or withhold, the mandate of those who will make decisions on their behalf.
Step 5 - If only one political party is contesting, the answer is No: there is no choice to be exercised, because every one of these questions has the same answer.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.stem: A Class 9 student is preparing notes on the laws that govern the conduct of elections in India. In steps, sort out which law deals with which part of the conduct of elections, and state which law lists the electoral offences and corrupt practices.

markingPoints.description: The Representation of the People Act, 1950 assigned to the allocation of seats and delimitation of constituencies (1)
The Representation of the People Act, 1950 assigned to the preparation and revision of electoral rolls (1)
The Representation of the People Act, 1950 ensures that every citizen over 18 years of age has the right to vote without discrimination (1)
The Representation of the People Act, 1951 assigned to nomination of candidates, election campaigns, voting procedures, resolution of disputes and post-election disputes (1)
The electoral offences and corrupt practices listed under the Representation of the People Act, 1951 (1)

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
Step 1 - The Representation of the People Act, 1950 (RPA, 1950) deals mainly with the allocation of seats and delimitation of constituencies.
Step 2 - It also deals with the preparation and revision of electoral rolls, and it ensures that every citizen over 18 years of age has the right to vote without discrimination.
Step 3 - The Representation of the People Act, 1951 (RPA, 1951) deals with all the other aspects of the conduct of elections and post-election disputes, laying down rules for nomination of candidates, election campaigns, voting procedures and resolution of disputes.
Step 4 - The Presidential and Vice-Presidential Elections Act, 1952 also exists.
Step 5 - The electoral offences and corrupt practices are listed by RPA, 1951, and together these Acts ensure the integrity, transparency and accountability of the electoral process.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.stem:
Two Class 9 students are arguing about whether a country may simply stop holding elections once its representatives have been chosen. One of them says that an election is not a single day but a process, and that in it the people do two things: they choose the representatives who will make decisions on their behalf, and they hold those representatives accountable. The other replies that regular and periodic elections lie at the core of democracy, and that the right to elect our representatives and to hold them accountable is ensured through periodic elections, with our vote as the principal means of exercising it.

(a) State the two things that the first student says the people do in an election. (b) Name the means by which we exercise the right to elect our representatives, and say what it is that periodic elections ensure. (c) The students then wonder whether their choice would still count if only one political party contested an election. Give the answer, and connect it to the two things named in part (a).

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
(a) The people choose those who will make decisions on their behalf, and they hold them accountable. (1)
(b) Our vote is the principal means by which we exercise this right, and periodic elections ensure that accountability. (2)
(c) No, because with only one party contesting there is no choice to be made at all. (1)

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.stem:
Gurmat was elected class representative in Grade 8, and when the new session begins some classmates ask whether she may simply stay on in Grade 9 without a fresh election, since the section already knows her. At the same time a student raises two further questions: whether a government that has completed its term may carry on without asking the people again, and whether the people can really choose if only one political party is contesting. Their teacher replies that all three questions have the same answer, and explains why.

(a) Give the answer that is required when a representative who was elected in Grade 8 is asked to carry on in Grade 9 without facing a fresh election, and the answer required when a government is asked to carry on beyond its prescribed term. (b) Name the element of democracy that these answers belong to, and say what it is that elected representatives are accountable to. (c) A third student points out that the same answer applies when only one political party is contesting. Explain why the answer must be the same in all three cases.

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
(a) No in both cases: a fresh election is needed, and a government cannot carry on beyond its prescribed term without seeking the mandate of the people again. (1)
(b) Participating in the periodic election of those who will make decisions on our behalf, one of the most crucial elements of democracy. (1)
(c) All three turn on one right: periodic elections let the people choose those who will decide for them and then hold them accountable. (2)
